chapter: Melvin Moore, Hammond and the New York trip
title: Hammond's caution about contracts and the drummer Clarence Dickson
summary: Hammond asks whether any member cannot be fired and says Joe Jones had spoiled him on drummers, while Fields' Clarence Dickson is lighter.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: over and everything and he asked me if I had anybody in the band who can't be fired? And I said no, but why do you ask that. He said, well, you know, a lot of you bands are doing all right but you can always use improvement. The next thing was, are you signed up with anybody? I said no. He said I just can't understand how somebody hasn't signed a band like you. He said, what I was thinking is I'll go and sign you, then somebody that signed a contract two years ago or something and hadn't done anything would come up and say that's my property. Then the next thing about it, you're clean, so you're at least living decent, but you're not making any money, and says, I don't like to get into something, if you have to make a change and you say now this man stuck with me when I wasn't doing anything and I can't feel that I should let him go. He said I don't like to get into those kinds of things. So I said, do you think somebody needs to be changed? He said no; I tell you one

thing though, I like the group, but Joe Jones kind of had me spoiled. He said when he dropped into New York way, he was kicking that Count Basie band, he says, we just hadn't had any drummers kicking no band like that unless it was Chick Webb that just kicked (inaudible).
Clarence Dickson; he was my drummer then.
So he was telling me nice, but I was just saying--
He was rather light, he's not as dynamic as Joe Jones.
